title: backups/<name>/backup.json
description: What a backup folder holds. The folder, backups/<yyyy-MM-dd-HHmmss>-<label>/ (a migration's: backups/<yyyy-MM-dd>-v<old version>/), mirrors the library's layout with the files copied before a migration, an import, an undo or a save that had to replace a file. Restoring copies them back and deletes absentFiles. Backups are safe to delete.

label.description: What the backup was taken for, as in the folder name: e.g. import, undo-import, prices, restore, conflict, unreadable, or v3 for a migration from version 3.

created.description: When it was taken, ISO 8601 to the second, e.g. 2026-09-30T14:25:01Z.

files.description: The files copied, as paths relative to the library folder.

absentFiles.description: Paths that didn't exist when the backup was taken; restoring deletes them, so an import that created a month file is fully undone.

schemaVersion.description: The library's format version when it was taken. A backup is only restored into a library with the same version.

result.description: After an edit that backed up the files it changed (an import, filling in past prices, a CLI prices or settings change, …): the same files as the edit wrote them, copied to result/, so undoing it leaves later edits in place. A backup without it is restored as it is.
